title: Compatibility adapter for tokenizer quirks and chat-template parsing during model onboarding
creator: Aisha Khan
description: During onboarding of community/open models we repeatedly see failures where the model's tokenizer or role delimiters in provided chat templates cause token-count mismatches, truncated streaming outputs, or incorrect structured output parsing. This ticket implements a compatibility adapter and onboarding checks so models can be admitted to the catalog without manual template/tokenizer surgery.
background: Incidents in recent onboarding runs (see links) show three recurring failure modes: 1) models that include unconventional special tokens (\u2018<|role|>\u2019 variants) that our tokenizer metadata doesn't declare, 2) chat templates that use mixed role delimiters (\u2018User:\u2019 vs \u2018<|user|>\u2019) leading to different token counts, and 3) models whose tokenizer splits role markers into subtokens causing structured output mismatch during evals and performance profile publishing. Manual fixes are time-consuming and lead to fragile onboarding documents.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a Tokenizer Compatibility Adapter: a lightweight shim that maps common legacy special tokens and normalizes unknown token IDs to canonical markers at the tokenizer layer. 2) Make the Chat Template Parser tolerant: detect common delimiter patterns and normalize them into our canonical internal role markers before token counting or prefix caching. 3) Onboarding Validator: generate an automated report that shows delta token counts (model tokenizer vs canonical), highlights risky templates, and optionally offers an automated remapping patch that can be applied after human review. 4) Publish canonicalized tokenization metadata into the model's onboarding artifact so performance profile generation uses the canonical counts. 5) Add unit + integration tests and a small benchmark showing end-to-end latency impact.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: Reduces manual intervention and onboarding cycle time; prevents regressions in profile publishing; maintains structured output invariants.
- Cons: Introduces a small runtime normalization cost at onboarding and at inference for patched models; risks masking bugs in model artifacts instead of forcing upstream fixes; increases surface area for tokenizer compatibility logic we must maintain.
- Mitigation: Adapter applied only at onboarding time and as an opt-in compatibility layer for hosted models; monitor adapter usage and add telemetry to decide long-term deprecation paths.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Tokenizer Compatibility Adapter merges to main and is exercised by unit tests covering at least 6 legacy token formats.
2) Chat Template Parser normalizes 4 known delimiter families and exposes a normalized template preview in the onboarding UI.
3) Onboarding Validator report produced automatically for all new model submissions and includes per-template delta token counts and suggested remapping.
4) Automated remapping patch can be applied via a single click in the console and creates a PR-like artifact for audit.
5) Performance profile publisher consumes canonicalized token counts and published profiles match offline ground-truth within 2% token count variance.
6) End-to-end latency regression from adding the adapter at serving is <5ms p50 for our standard micro-benchmark and documented in the release notes.
7) Docs updated and a short runbook created for agents/support to handle edge cases.
